questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of oscillation of a mass $m$ suspended by a spring is $v_1$. If the length of the spring is cut to half, the same mass oscillates with frequency $v_2$. The value of $v_2/v_1$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The frequency of oscillation of a spring-mass system is given by $v = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$, where $k$ is the spring constant and $m$ is the mass.

The spring constant $k$ is inversely proportional to the length of the spring $L$, so $k \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

When the length of the spring is cut to half, the new length is $L' = \dfrac{L}{2}$. The new spring constant becomes $k' = 2k$.

The new frequency of oscillation is $v_2 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{k'}{m}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{2k}{m}} = \sqrt{2} v_1$.

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring stretches by $2$ mm when it is loaded with a mass of $200$ g. From equilibrium position the mass is further pulled down by $2$ mm and released. The frequency associated with the system and maximum energy in the spring are __________ Hz and __________ J, respectively. (Take g $= 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
At equilibrium, the restoring force of the spring balances the weight of the mass:

$mg = kx_0$

$k = \dfrac{mg}{x_0} = \dfrac{0.2 \times 10}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 1000$ N/m

The frequency of oscillation is given by:

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{1000}{0.2}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{5000} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{50}}{2\pi} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{50}}{\pi}$ Hz

The maximum energy in the spring corresponds to its maximum elastic potential energy, which occurs at the maximum extension.

Maximum extension $x_{max} = x_0 + A = 2 \text{ mm} + 2 \text{ mm} = 4 \text{ mm} = 4 \times 10^{-3}$ m

Maximum energy in the spring $U_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2} k x_{max}^2$

$U_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1000 \times (4 \times 10^{-3})^2$

$U_{max} = 500 \times 16 \times 10^{-6} = 8000 \times 10^{-6} = 8 \times 10^{-3}$ J

Answer: $\dfrac{5\sqrt{50}}{\pi}$ and $8 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is $A$ and time period is $5$ sec. The time required by it to move from $x = A$ to $x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$ is _______ sec.
questions.solution:
The equation of simple harmonic motion for a particle starting from the extreme position $x = A$ is given by:

$x = A \cos(\omega t)$

We need to find the time $t$ when the particle reaches $x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$. Substituting this value into the equation:

$\dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}} = A \cos(\omega t)$

$\cos(\omega t) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Since the angular frequency $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, we have:

$\dfrac{2\pi}{T} t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$t = \dfrac{T}{8}$

Given the time period $T = 5$ sec, the required time is:

$t = \dfrac{5}{8}$ sec

Answer: $5/8$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. $\sin^2 \omega t$I. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ but not simple harmonic motion (SHM)
B. $\sin^3(2\omega t)$II. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ but Not SHM
C. $\sin(\omega t) + \cos(\pi \omega t)$III. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ and SHM
D. $\cos\omega t + \cos 2\omega t$IV. Non-periodic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For A: $y = \sin^2 \omega t = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\omega t}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \cos 2\omega t$

This represents simple harmonic motion (SHM) about the mean position $y = \dfrac{1}{2}$ with an angular frequency of $2\omega$. The time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, A matches III.

For B: $y = \sin^3(2\omega t) = \dfrac{3\sin 2\omega t - \sin 6\omega t}{4}$

This is a superposition of two SHMs with angular frequencies $2\omega$ and $6\omega$. It is periodic but not SHM. The time period is the LCM of $T_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ and $T_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{6\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{3\omega}$, which is $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, B matches I.

For C: $y = \sin(\omega t) + \cos(\pi \omega t)$

The angular frequencies are $\omega_1 = \omega$ and $\omega_2 = \pi \omega$. The ratio $\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2} = \dfrac{1}{\pi}$ is an irrational number. Therefore, the function is non-periodic. Thus, C matches IV.

For D: $y = \cos \omega t + \cos 2\omega t$

This is a superposition of two SHMs with angular frequencies $\omega$ and $2\omega$. It is periodic but not SHM. The time period is the LCM of $T_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ and $T_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$, which is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, D matches II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A uniform disc of radius $R$ and mass $M$ is free to oscillate about the axis $A$ as shown in the figure. For small oscillations the time period is ______.
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
From the given figure, the axis of rotation is a horizontal line passing through the point $A$ on the edge of the disc. The circular arrow around the axis indicates that the disc oscillates out of its plane, meaning the axis of rotation is a tangent to the disc in its own plane.

The moment of inertia of a uniform disc about its diameter is $I_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{4}MR^2$.

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the disc about the given axis of rotation is:
$I = I_{cm} + MR^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{5}{4}MR^2$

The distance from the center of mass of the disc to the axis of rotation is $d = R$.

The time period of a physical pendulum is given by:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{Mgd}}$

Substituting the values of $I$ and $d$:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{5}{4}MR^2}{MgR}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{5R}{4g}}$

Answer: $2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{5R}{4g}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity of a particle executing simple harmonic motion along $x$-axis is described as $v^2 = 50 - x^2$, where $x$ represents displacement. If the time period of motion is $\dfrac{x}{7}$ s, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The given equation is $v^2 = 50 - x^2$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$2v \dfrac{dv}{dx} = -2x$

$v \dfrac{dv}{dx} = -x$

Since acceleration $a = v \dfrac{dv}{dx}$, we get:

$a = -x$

Comparing this with the standard equation of SHM $a = -\omega^2 x$, we get:

$\omega^2 = 1 \Rightarrow \omega = 1$ rad/s

The time period of the motion is given by:

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi$

Taking $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$, we get:

$T = 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} = \dfrac{44}{7}$ s

Given that the time period is $\dfrac{x}{7}$ s, comparing the two gives:

$x = 44$

Answer: $44$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equation of motion of a particle is given by $x = a \sin\left(50t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ cm. The particle will come to rest at time $t_1$ and it will have zero acceleration at time $t_2$. The $t_1$ and $t_2$ respectively are _______.
questions.solution:
The equation of motion is given by $x = a \sin\left(50t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$.

Velocity is the rate of change of displacement:
$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 50a \cos\left(50t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

The particle comes to rest when $v = 0$. For the first time it comes to rest:
$\cos\left(50t_1 + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 0$

$50t_1 + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$50t_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$t_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{300} \text{ s}$

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity:
$A = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = -2500a \sin\left(50t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

The particle has zero acceleration when $A = 0$. For the first time it has zero acceleration:
$\sin\left(50t_2 + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 0$

$50t_2 + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \pi$

$50t_2 = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

$t_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{150} = \dfrac{\pi}{75} \text{ s}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{300} \, s, \dfrac{\pi}{75} \, s$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time period of a simple harmonic oscillator is $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$. Measured value of mass $(m)$ of the object is 10 g with an accuracy of 10 mg and time for 50 oscillations of the spring is found to be 60 s using a watch of 2 s resolution. Percentage error in determination of spring constant $(k)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ \%.
questions.solution:
The given formula for time period is
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$.
Squaring both sides, we get $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \frac{k}{m}$, which gives $k = \frac{4\pi^2 m}{T^2}$.
The relative error in $k$ is given by $\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\frac{\Delta T}{T}$.
Given: $m = 10$ g, $\Delta m = 10$ mg $= 0.01$ g.
Total time for $n=50$ oscillations is $t = 60$ s with resolution $\Delta t = 2$ s.
Since $T = t/n$, the relative error in $T$ is the same as in $t$: $\frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{\Delta t}{t}$.
Substituting the values: $\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{0.01}{10} + 2\left(\frac{2}{60}\right)$.
$\frac{\Delta k}{k} = 0.001 + \frac{2}{30} = 0.001 + 0.0666...$
Percentage error $= \left(0.001 + \frac{1}{15}\right) \times 100 = 0.1 + \frac{100}{15} = 0.1 + 6.666... = 6.766...\%$.
Rounding to two decimal places, we get $6.76\%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: As shown in the figure, a spring is kept in a stretched position with some extension by holding the masses 1 kg and 0.2 kg with a separation more than spring natural length and are released. Assuming the horizontal surface to be frictionless, the angular frequency (in SI unit) of the system is : $k=150 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$
questions.solution:
Two masses (1 kg and 0.2 kg) connected by a spring (k = 150 N/m) on a frictionless surface undergo oscillation about their center of mass.
This two-body problem reduces to SHM with reduced mass $\mu = \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{1 \times 0.2}{1.2} = \frac{1}{6}$ kg.
The angular frequency is $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{150}{1/6}} = \sqrt{900} = 30$ rad/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The displacement of a particle, executing simple harmonic motion with time period $T$, is expressed as $x(t)=A \sin \omega t$, where $A$ is the amplitude. The maximum value of potential energy of this oscillator is found at $t=T / 2 \beta$. The value of $\beta$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For SHM with $x(t) = A\sin(\omega t)$, the potential energy is
$U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 \sin^2(\omega t)$.
Maximum potential energy occurs when $\sin^2(\omega t) = 1$, i.e., when $\omega t = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}, ...$
The first maximum occurs at $\omega t = \frac{\pi}{2}$, giving $t = \frac{\pi}{2\omega} = \frac{\pi}{2} \cdot \frac{T}{2\pi} = \frac{T}{4}$.
Since this is given as $t = \frac{T}{2\beta}$.
We have $\frac{T}{4} = \frac{T}{2\beta}$, so $\beta = 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylindrical block of mass $M$ and area of cross section $A$ is floating in a liquid of density $\rho$ and with its axis vertical. When depressed a little and released the block starts oscillating. The period of oscillation is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
When the block is depressed by distance $x$, the additional buoyant force is $F = \rho Agx$ acting upward as restoring force.
Equation of motion: $M\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -\rho Agx$.
This gives $\omega^2 = \frac{\rho Ag}{M}$.
Period of oscillation: $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{M}{\rho Ag}}$

Period of oscillation: $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{M}{\rho Ag}}$

questions.q: Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are attached to the ends of springs $A$ and $B$ as shown in figure. The energy stored in $A$ is $E$. The energy stored in $B$, when spring constants $k_{A}, k_{B}$ of $A$ and $B$, respectively satisfy the relation $4 k_{A}=3 k_{B^{\prime}}$, is :
questions.solution:
For blocks hanging in equilibrium, spring extensions are:
$x_A = \frac{m_A g}{k_A} = \frac{100g}{k_A}$ and $x_B = \frac{m_B g}{k_B} = \frac{200g}{k_B}$.
Energy stored:
$E = \frac{1}{2}k_A x_A^2 = \frac{5000g^2}{k_A}$ and $U_B = \frac{1}{2}k_B x_B^2 = \frac{20000g^2}{k_B}$.
Taking ratio: $\frac{U_B}{E} = 4 \cdot \frac{k_A}{k_B}$.
Given $4k_A = 3k_B$, we have $\frac{k_A}{k_B} = \frac{3}{4}$.
Therefore: $U_B = 4E \cdot \frac{3}{4} = 3E$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple pendulum of string length 30 cm performs 20 oscillations in 10 s. The length of the string required for the pendulum to perform 40 oscillations in the same time duration is $\_\_\_\_$ cm. [Assume that the mass of the pendulum remains same.]
questions.solution:
Period of simple pendulum: $T = \frac{\text{time}}{\text{number of oscillations}}$
Initial period: $T_1 = \frac{10}{20} = 0.5$ s
Required period: $T_2 = \frac{10}{40} = 0.25$ s
Using $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$, the ratio is: $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \sqrt{\frac{L_2}{L_1}}$
$\frac{0.25}{0.5} = \sqrt{\frac{L_2}{30}} \Rightarrow 0.5 = \sqrt{\frac{L_2}{30}}$
$0.25 = \frac{L_2}{30} \Rightarrow L_2 = 7.5$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Using a simple pendulum experiment $g$ is determind by measuring its time period $T$. Which of the following plots represent the correct relation between the pendulum length $L$ and time period $T$ ?
questions.solution:
The time period $T$ of a simple pendulum of length $L$ is given by the formula:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$
Squaring both sides, we get:
$T^2 = 4\pi^2 \frac{L}{g}$
Rearranging the equation to find the relationship between $\frac{1}{T^2}$ and $L$:
$\frac{1}{T^2} = \frac{g}{4\pi^2 L}$
Let $y = \frac{1}{T^2}$ and $x = L$. The equation becomes:
$y = \frac{k}{x}$ where $k = \frac{g}{4\pi^2}$ is a constant.
This is the equation of a rectangular hyperbola in the first quadrant.
As $L$ increases, $\frac{1}{T^2}$ decreases non-linearly, approaching the axes asymptotically.
Comparing this with the given plots, option (2) correctly represents a hyperbolic relationship between $\frac{1}{T^2}$ and $L$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of $176 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is $\_\_\_\_$ Hz. $\left[\right.$ take $\left.\pi=\frac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.solution:
In a simple harmonic oscillator, if the displacement is $x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$, the velocity is $v = A\omega \cos(\omega t + \phi)$.
The kinetic energy is given by $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)$.
Using the identity $\cos^2 \theta = \frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}$, we get $K = \frac{1}{4}m A^2 \omega^2 [1 + \cos(2\omega t + 2\phi)]$.
The angular frequency of the kinetic energy oscillation is $\omega_{KE} = 2\omega$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency of the SHM.
Given $\omega_{KE} = 176$ rad/s, we have $2\omega = 176$, which gives $\omega = 88$ rad/s.
The frequency of the simple harmonic oscillator is $f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}$.
Substituting the values: $f = \frac{88}{2 \times \frac{22}{7}} = \frac{88 \times 7}{44} = 2 \times 7 = 14$ Hz.

questions.q:
Two blocks of masses $m$ and $M,(M \gt m)$, are placed on a frictionless table as shown in figure. A massless spring with spring constant k is attached with the lower block. If the system is slightly displaced and released then
($\mu=$ coefficient of friction between the two blocks)

(A) The time period of small oscillation of the two blocks is $\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{M})}{\mathrm{k}}}$
(B) The acceleration of the blocks is $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{kx}}{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}$ ($\mathrm{x}=$ displacement of the blocks from the mean position)
(C) The magnitude of the frictional force on the upper block is $\frac{m \mu|x|}{M+m}$
(D) The maximum amplitude of the upper block, if it does not slip, is $\frac{\mu(M+m) g}{k}$
(E) Maximum frictional force can be $\mu(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}) \mathrm{g}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) As both blocks moving together so Time period $=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~m}}{\mathrm{~K}}} ;$ where $\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}$
$\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{~K}}}$
(B) Let block is displaced by x in $(+\mathrm{ve})$ direction so force on block will be in(-ve) direction
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{F}=-\mathrm{Kx} \\ & (\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}) \mathrm{a}=-\mathrm{Kx} \\ & \mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{Kx}}{(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m})}
\end{aligned}$
(C) As upper block is moving due to friction thus
$\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma}=\frac{\mathrm{mKx}}{(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m})}$
(D) This option is like two block problem in friction for maximum amplitude, force on block is also maximum, for which both blocks are moving together.

$\begin{aligned}
& K A=(M+m) a \\ & a=\frac{K A}{(M+m)} \\ & f=m a=\frac{m K A}{(M+m)} \\ & f_{\max }=f_L=\mu \mathrm{mg} \\ & f=\mu m g \\ & \frac{m K A}{(M+m)}=\mu m g \\ & A=\frac{\mu(M+m) g}{K}
\end{aligned}$
(E) Maximum friction can be $\mu \mathrm{mg}$ as force is acting between blocks \& normal force here is mg.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Knowing initial position $x_0$ and initial momentum $p_0$ is enough to determine the position and momentum at any time $t$ for a simple harmonic motion with a given angular frequency $\omega$.
Reason (R): The amplitude and phase can be expressed in terms of $x_0$ and $\mathrm{p}_0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ If we express position } x(t)=A \sin (\omega t+\phi) \\ & \text{ then } x_0=A \sin \phi \\ & v_0=A \omega \cos \phi \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \phi=\frac{\omega x_0}{v_0} \\ & A=\sqrt{x_0^2+\frac{v_0^2}{\omega^2}}\end{aligned}$
Hence both position and linear momentum of a particle can be expressed as a function of time if we know initial momentum and position

Assertion (A) : A simple pendulum is taken to a planet of mass and radius, 4 times and 2 times, respectively, than the Earth. The time period of the pendulum remains same on earth and the planet.
Reason (R): The mass of the pendulum remains unchanged at Earth and the other planet.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& g=\frac{G M}{R^2} \\
& g^{\prime}=\frac{G(4 M)}{(2 R)^2}=g
\end{aligned}$

A is correct, $R$ is correct ; but since $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g}}$ doesn't depend on mass ; R doesn't explain A .

& \mathrm{v}=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A mass $m$ is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency ${f}_{1} .$ The frequency of oscillations if a mass $9m$ is suspended from the same spring is ${f}_{2} .$ The value of $\dfrac{{f}_{1}}{{f}_{2}}$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Frequency of oscillation of a spring-block system is given by, $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Therefore, for both cases, we can write

${f}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$ and 

${f}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{9m}}$

Required ratio, $\dfrac{{f}_{1}}{{f}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{1}} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

questions.q: The time period of simple harmonic motion of mass $M$ in the given figure is $\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\alphaM}{5K}}$, where the value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.solution:
For series combination of the spring, equivalent spring constant is given by, $\dfrac{1}{{k}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{k}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{2}}$.

Therefore, for combined system net spring constant ${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{2k \times k}{2k + k} + k = \dfrac{5k}{3}$

Angular frequency of oscillation $\left(\omega\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{eq}}{m}}$

$⇒ \left(\omega\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{5k}{3m}}$

Period of oscillation $\left(τ\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3m}{5k}}$

$= \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{12m}{5k}}$

Therefore, $\alpha = 12$.

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\dfrac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\dfrac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Speed in SHM in terms of displacement is given by, $v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}}$.

at $x = \dfrac{2A}{3}$, we get

$v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}A\omega}{3}$

Let the new amplitude be$= A '$

Then, 

$v ' = 3v ⇒ \omega\sqrt{{\left(A '\right)}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5}A\omega$

$⇒ A ' = \dfrac{7}{3}A$

Therefore, $n = 7$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is $4m$, then the time period of small oscillations will be _________$s$.

$[$take $g = {\pi}^{2}m{s}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at surface of earth, $g = \dfrac{GM}{{R}^{2}}$.

Now, at distance $R$ from the surface of the earth, ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{GM}{{\left(R + R\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{g}{4}$

Therefore,
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{g}{4}}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 4}{g}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\dfrac{4}{\pi} = 8s$

questions.q: A simple harmonic oscillator has an amplitude $A$ and time period $6\pi$ second. Assuming the oscillation starts from its mean position, the time required by it to travel from$x = A$ to $x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}A$ will be $\dfrac{\pi}{x}s$, where $x = _______ .$
questions.solution:
From phasor diagram particle has to move from $P$ to $Q$ in a circle of radius equal to amplitude of $SHM$.

$cosϕ = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}A}{2}}{A} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Now, $\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \omegat$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}t$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{2\pi}{6\pi}t$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

So, $x = 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is $\dfrac{x}{8}$, where $x =$_________.
questions.solution:
The total energy of the harmonic oscillator is given by the formula

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}k{A}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, $k$ is the force constant and $A$ is the amplitude.

The potential energy of the oscillator at the given displacement can be written as

$\begin{cases}U & = & \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right)}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{k{A}^{2}}{2 \times 9} \\ & = & \dfrac{E}{9}\end{cases}$

Hence, its kinetic energy is given by

$\begin{cases}KE & = & E - \dfrac{E}{9} \\ & = & \dfrac{8E}{9}\end{cases}$

Thus, the required ratio is

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{E}{KE} & = & \dfrac{E}{\dfrac{8E}{9}} \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{8}\end{cases}$

Hence, $x = 9$.

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $4cm$. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is $10cm{s}^{- 1}$. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes $5cm{s}^{- 1}$ is $\sqrt{\alpha}cm$, where $\alpha =$______.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at the mean position is given by

$V = A\omega . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$10 = 4 \times \omega ⇒ \omega = \dfrac{5}{2}rad{s}^{- 1}$

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at any instantaneous position $x$ can be expressed as

$v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation (2), it follows that

$5 = \dfrac{5}{2}\sqrt{{4}^{2} - {x}^{2}} ⇒ {x}^{2} = 16 - 4 = 12 ⇒ x = \sqrt{12}cm$

Hence, $\alpha = 12$.

Hence, $\alpha = 12$.

questions.q:
In a linear Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)

(A) Restoring force is directly proportional to the displacement.

(B) The acceleration and displacement are opposite in direction.

(C) The velocity is maximum at mean position.

(D) The acceleration is minimum at extreme points.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The equations of SHM is given by

$F = – kx$

$⇒ a = – {\omega}^{2}x$

Velocity is given by, $v = \omega\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}}$.

Clearly, velocity is maximum at mean position and acceleration is maximum at extreme positions.

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM of amplitude$A$. The distance from the mean position when its kinetic energy becomes equal to its potential energy is:
questions.solution:
The potential energy is given by

$U = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2}}{2}$

The kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2} ( {A}^{2} - {x}^{2} )}{2}$.

Using the condition that $K = U$,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}\left({A}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: Which graph represents the difference between total energy and potential energy of a particle executing $SHM$ vs its distance from mean position?
questions.solution:
In a SHM, mechanical energy is conserved. So, the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy remains constant.

For a SHM,

$T . E . - U = K . E$

$⇒ T . E . - U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}\left({A}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right)$

This is the equation of a downward parabola.

questions.q: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion (SHM). The ratio of potential energy and kinetic energy of the particle when its displacement is half of its amplitude will be
questions.solution:

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) to obtain the required ratio.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{P}{K} & = & \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}^{2}}{{A}^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}^{2}} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{3}\end{cases}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular block of mass $5kg$ attached to a horizontal spiral spring executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude $1m$ and time period $3 . 14s$. The maximum force exerted by spring on block is ___ $N$.
questions.solution:
By Newton's second law,

$F = m{a}_{max}$.

The maximum acceleration for a SHM is given by

${a}_{max} = {\omega}^{2}A . . . ( i )$

The time period is given by

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 3 . 14s$

$⇒ \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3 . 14} = 2rad{s}^{- 1}$

Thus, the maximum acceleration from equation (i)

${a}_{max} = 4 \times 1 = 4m{s}^{- 2}$

The maximum force is

$F = 5kg \times 4m{s}^{- 2} = 20N$

questions.q: For particle $P$ revolving round the centre $O$ with radius of circular path $r$ and regular velocity $\omega$, as shown in below figure, the projection of $OP$ on the $x$-axis at time $t$ is
questions.solution:
As can be seen from the diagram, the initial phase of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}\phi & = & 30 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{\pi}{6}\end{cases}$

The equation of motion of the particle at its initial position at time $t = 0$ can be written as

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\theta . . . ( 1 )$

where, $\theta$ is the angular displacement of the particle at time $t = t$.

Since, the position of the particle at a later instant of time always lags behind its initial position at time $t = 0$, the equation of motion of the particle at any instant of time is given by

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\left(\theta + \phi\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

$x ( t ) = rcos\left(\omegat + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

questions.q: A simple pendulum with length $100cm$ and bob of mass $250g$ is executing S.H.M of amplitude $10cm$. The maximum tension in the string is found to be $\dfrac{x}{40}N$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
From the given figure we can see that

$sin{\theta}_{0} = \dfrac{A}{l} = \dfrac{10}{100} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

From conservation of energy $\dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = mgl ( 1 - cos{\theta}_{0} )$

Maximum tension occurs at mean position

$T = mg + \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{l} ⇒ T = mg + 2mg ( 1 - cos{\theta}_{0} )$

Substituting the values,

$T = mg ( 1 + 2 ( 1 - \sqrt{1 - \sin^{2}{\theta}_{0}} ) ⇒ T = mg ( 3 - 2\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{100}} ) ⇒ T = 0 . 25 \times 9 . 8 ( 3 - 2 ( 1 - \dfrac{1}{200} ) ) ⇒ T = 0 . 25 \times 9 . 8 \times 1 . 01 = 2 . 4745N$

It is given that

$T = \dfrac{x}{40} ⇒ x = 40 \times 2 . 4745 = 98 . 98 \approx 99$

Equation (2) suggests that the graph between the square of the time period versus the length of the pendulum is a straight line passing through the origin.

questions.q: The amplitude of a particle executing SHM is $3cm$. The displacement at which its kinetic energy will be $25 %$ more than the potential energy is: ______ $cm$.
questions.solution:
Let $x$ be the displacement at which its kinetic energy will be $25 %$ more than the potential energy.

Given here, $A = 3cm$ and $KE = PE + \dfrac{PE}{4}$

So, $KE = \dfrac{5}{4}PE$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}\left({A}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} - {x}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}{x}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{9{x}^{2}}{4} = {A}^{2}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{3}A$

$∴ x = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 3cm$

$⇒ x = 2cm$

questions.q: In the figure given below. a block of mass $M = 490g$ placed on a frictionless table is connected with two springs having same spring constant ($K = 2N{m}^{- 1}$). If the block is horizontally displaced through $X$m$ then the number of complete oscillations it will make in $14\pi$ seconds will be ______.
questions.solution:
Both the springs are connected in parallel, therefore

${K}_{eq} = K + K = 2K$

Now, time period of spring-block system is given by,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2K}}$

Given here, $m = 490gm$= 0 . 49kg$ and $K = 2N{m}^{- 1}$

So, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 49}{2 \times 2}}$

$= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{49}{400}} = 2\pi\dfrac{7}{20} = \dfrac{7\pi}{10}$

Now, number of oscillation in $14\pi$ is

$N = \dfrac{time}{T} = \dfrac{14\pi}{\dfrac{7\pi}{10}} = 20$

questions.q: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is $x = Asin\omegat$. Let $T$ be its time period. The slope of its potential energy ($U$) – time ($t$) curve will be maximum when $t = \dfrac{T}{\beta}$. The value of $\beta$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Given here, displacement $x = Asin\left(\omegat\right)$

Now, potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is $U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat\right)$,

So, slope of potential energy and time curve is $\dfrac{dU}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{\omega}^{3}{A}^{2}}{2}sin2\omegat$

Now, ${\left(\dfrac{dU}{dt}\right)}_{max}$ will be maximum when $sin2\omegat = 1$

$⇒ 2\omegat = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ t = \dfrac{T}{8} ⇒ \beta = 8$

questions.explanation:
Given here, displacement $x = Asin\left(\omegat\right)$

Now, potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is $U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat\right)$,

So, slope of potential energy and time curve is $\dfrac{dU}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{\omega}^{3}{A}^{2}}{2}sin2\omegat$

Now, ${\left(\dfrac{dU}{dt}\right)}_{max}$ will be maximum when $sin2\omegat = 1$

$⇒ 2\omegat = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ t = \dfrac{T}{8} ⇒ \beta = 8$

questions.q: Two simple harmonic waves having equal amplitudes of $8cm$ and equal frequency of $10Hz$ are moving along the same direction. The resultant amplitude is also $8cm$. The phase difference between the individual waves is _____ degree.
questions.solution:
If two waves have the same amplitude, frequency, and direction, but are out of phase by $ϕ$ degrees, then the amplitude of the resultant waves is given by ${A}_{R} = 2Acos\left(\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2}\right)$

Here, ${A}_{1} = {A}_{2} = {A}_{R} = 8cm$

So, $cos\left(\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Or phase difference between the individual waves is $\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2} = 60 ° ⇒ \Deltaϕ = 120 °$.

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x = – A\text{and}x = + A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x = 0$ to $\dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2s$; then time taken by particle in going from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
questions.solution:
The position of a particle performing an SHM is given by:

$x = Asin ( \omegat + ϕ )$

Since at $t = 0s$, the particle is at $x = 0$, therefore the initial phase $ϕ = 0$.

At time $t = 2s$, the particle is at $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$.

$∴ \dfrac{A}{2} = Asin\left(2\omega\right) ⇒ \omega = \dfrac{\pi}{12}{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, time period

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 24s$

The total time taken from $x = 0$ to $x = A$ is $\dfrac{T}{4} = 6s$.

Since the time taken from $x = 0$ to $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2s$, therefore the time taken from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $x = A$ is $4s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $m$ attached to free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of $1s$. If the mass is increased by $3kg$ the period of oscillation increases by one second, the value of mass $m$ is ________ $kg$.
questions.solution:
Time period of oscillation is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$, where $k$ is the force constant of the spring.

$∵$ Spring is same, therefore, spring constant will be same.

Putting the different values,

In the first case $T = 1 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

In the second case ${T}^{'} = 2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m + 3}{k}}$

Dividing the equations, we get

$\dfrac{T}{{T}^{'}} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{m + 3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{m + 3} = \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ 4m = m + 3 ⇒ m = 1$

Thus, $m = 1kg$

questions.q: The metallic bob of simple pendulum has the relative density $5$. The time period of this pendulum is $10s$. If the metallic bob is immersed in water, then the new time period becomes $5\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
When the bob is immersed in water its effective weight is $m{g}^{'} = mg - {F}_{B}$, where, ${F}_{B}$ is buoyant force.

Then, ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{mg - {F}_{B}}{m}$= \dfrac{{ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{W}Vg}{{ρ}_{B}V}$

$= \left(\dfrac{{ρ}_{B} - {ρ}_{w}}{{ρ}_{B}}\right)g$= \dfrac{5 - 1}{5} \times g$= \dfrac{4}{5}g$

Now, time period of simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

Thus, the ratio $\dfrac{{T}^{'}}{T} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{{g}^{'}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\dfrac{4}{5}g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}}$

$⇒ {T}^{'} = T\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{10}{2}\sqrt{5}$

Thus, the new time period is ${T}^{'} = 5\sqrt{5}s$.

Hence, value of $x = 5$.

questions.q: The time period of oscillation of a simple pendulum of length $L$ suspended from the roof of a vehicle, which moves without friction down an inclined plane of inclination $\alpha$, is given by :
questions.solution:
Acceleration of vehicle down the incline will be $a = gsin\alpha$
In the frame of the vehicle, we have to apply pseudo force. The Force diagram is shown in figure.

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{{g}_{eff}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g cos \alpha}}$.

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle of mass $4kg$ in motion along the $x$-axis is given by $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$. The time period of the particle for small oscillation $\left(sin\theta ≃ \theta\right) \left(\dfrac{\pi}{K}\right)s$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Given here, potential energy, $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy, $F = - \dfrac{d U}{d x}$.

We have, $F = - 4\left(+ sin4x\right)4 = - 16sin\left(4x\right)$

For small $\theta$, $sin\theta \approx \theta$.

Acceleration of particle is $a = - \dfrac{64x}{m} = \dfrac{- 64x}{4} = - 16x$

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so $a = - {\omega}^{2}x ⇒ {\omega}^{2} = 16 ⇒ \omega = 4rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, time period of oscillation is$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Thus, the value of $K = 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $0 . 9kg$, attached to a horizontal spring, executes SHM with an amplitude ${A}_{1}$. When this mass passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass of $124g$ is placed over it and both masses move together with amplitude ${A}_{2}$. If the ratio $\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}}$ is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1}$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
At mean position, the velocity of the particle in S.H.M. is maximum, so kinetic energy is $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}k{A}^{2}$, where, $k$ is spring constant.

We also know that, kinetic energy is related to momentum as $KE = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$.

Now, from both equations, we have

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{A}^{2} = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$ (Here, momentum is conserved)

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1}} = \dfrac{1024}{900}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{32}{30} = \dfrac{16}{15} = \dfrac{16}{16 - 1}$

$∴ \alpha = 16$

questions.q: As per given figures, two springs of spring constants $K$ and $2K$ are connected to mass $m$. If the period of oscillation in figure (a) is $3s$, then the period of oscillation in figure (b) will be $\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
In figure (a), the springs are connected in series. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}} = \dfrac{K \times 2K}{K + 2K} = \dfrac{2K}{3}$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{a} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\dfrac{2K}{3}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3m}{2K}}$

In figure (b), the springs are connected in parallel. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = {K}_{1} + {K}_{2} = 3K$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{b} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{3K}}$

Now,

$\dfrac{{T}_{a}}{{T}_{b}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{2}} ⇒ {T}_{b} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}{T}_{a} = \sqrt{2}s$

Hence, $x = 2$

questions.q: When a particle executes simple Harmonic motion, the nature of graph of velocity as function of displacement will be
questions.solution:
The displacement equation of a particle is given by

$x = Asin\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) ⇒ sin\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) = \dfrac{x}{A}$

The velocity equation is given by,

$v = \omegaAcos\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) ⇒ cos\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) = \dfrac{v}{\omegaA}$

Since, $\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{A}^{2}} + \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2}} = 1$

The above equation represents an ellipse.

$⇒ cosϕ = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ ϕ = 60 °$

Time period of a simple pendulum in a stationary lift is $T$. If the lift accelerates with $\dfrac{g}{6}$ vertically upwards then the time period will be
(Where $g =$ acceleration due to gravity)

The time period of a simple pendulum is given by$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

In an upward accelerating frame the effective ${g}_{eff} = g + a$

$\dfrac{T}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g + \dfrac{g}{6}}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{6}}$

$⇒ {T}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{7}}T$

Maximum velocity is given by ${v}_{max} = \omegaA$= \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}A$

Here, $\sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{1}}{{m}_{1}}}{A}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{{m}_{2}}}{A}_{2}$

$⇒ 2{A}_{1} = 3{A}_{2}$

Thus, ratio of amplitude is $\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2} = 3: 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
For a body executing S.H.M. :
(a) Potential energy is always equal to its $K . E .$
(b) Average potential and kinetic energy over any given time interval are always equal.
(c) Sum of the kinetic and potential energy at any point of time is constant.
(d) Average $K . E .$ in one time period is equal to average potential energy in one time period.
Choose the most appropriate option from the options given below :
questions.solution: The formula of kinetic energy in S.H.M. is, $K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{\left(\sqrt{{A}^{2} - {x}^{2}}\right)}^{2}$, where $A$ is the amplitude of the S.H.M. the formula of potential energy is, $P . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2}$, so the net energy is defined as, $T . E . = P . E . + K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2}$ so the total energy is always constant. Since, energy changes from potential to kinetic and vice-versa the average $K . E .$ in one time period is equal to the average $P . E .$ in one time period.

Springs are in series connection,

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{0 . 16}} = \sqrt{100} = 10$

Time period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega '}$

Angular frequency of SHM

The point $A$ covers $30 ° in 0 . 1s$.
Then, we have $\dfrac{\pi}{6}rad ⟶ 0 . 1s$.
Or $1rad ⟶ \dfrac{0 . 1}{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}s$
Or $2\piin \to \dfrac{0 . 1 \times 6}{\pi} \times 2\pi$
Thus, time taken is $T = 1 . 2sec .

We know that $\omega = $\dfrac{2\pi}{T}
Then, $\omega = $\dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}
Restoration force $( F ) = {m \omega}^{2}A .

Then Restoration force per unit mass $\left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = {\omega}^{2}A$
$\left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = {\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}\right)}^{2} \times 0 . 36$

$≅ 9 . 87N$

questions.q: A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without slipping or sliding (i) in its plane with a time period ${T}_{1}$ and (ii) back and forth in a direction perpendicular to its plane, with a period ${T}_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}}$ will be :
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillation of physical pendulum is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{Mgl}} . . . ( 1 )$

Where, $I$ is the moment of inertia of ring about given axis and $l$ is the distance of centre of mass of ring from the axis of rotation.

Moment of inertia of ring in its plane is given by

${I}_{1} = {I}_{c} + M{d}^{2} = M{R}^{2} + M{R}^{2} = 2M{R}^{2}$

Moment of inertia of ring perpendicular to its plane is given by

${I}_{2} = {I}_{c} + M{d}^{2} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} + M{R}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}M{R}^{2}$

Now the ratio of time period is given by

$\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2M{R}^{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}M{R}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$
questions.question: A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without slipping or sliding (i) in its plane with a time period ${T}_{1}$ and (ii) back and forth in a direction perpendicular to its plane, with a period ${T}_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}}$ will be :
questions.explanation:
The time period of oscillation of physical pendulum is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{Mgl}} . . . ( 1 )$

Where, $I$ is the moment of inertia of ring about given axis and $l$ is the distance of centre of mass of ring from the axis of rotation.

Moment of inertia of ring in its plane is given by

${I}_{1} = {I}_{c} + M{d}^{2} = M{R}^{2} + M{R}^{2} = 2M{R}^{2}$

Moment of inertia of ring perpendicular to its plane is given by

${I}_{2} = {I}_{c} + M{d}^{2} = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} + M{R}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}M{R}^{2}$

Now the ratio of time period is given by

$\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2M{R}^{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}M{R}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: A simple pendulum oscillating in air has period $T$ . The bob of the pendulum is completely immersed in a non-viscous liquid. The density of the liquid is $\dfrac{1}{16}th$ of the material of the bob. If the bob is inside liquid all the time, its period of oscillation in this liquid is:
questions.solution:
Let the density of bob is $\sigma$ & density of liquid is $\dfrac{\sigma}{16}$ .
Now, Net downward force on bob = Weight - Buoyancy
$= \sigmaVg - \dfrac{\sigma}{16}Vg = \dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg$
Net effective gravitational acceleration $= \dfrac{\dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg}{\sigmaV} = \dfrac{15}{16}g$
Time period $\left(T\right) = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{{g}_{eff}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{15}{16}g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}\dfrac{l}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}} ∙ \left(2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{15}}T$
$= 4T\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{15}}$

questions.q: A rod of mass $M$ and length $2L$ is suspended at its middle by a wire. It exhibits torsional oscillations. If two masses, each of mass $m$, are attached at a distance $L / 2$ from its centre on both sides, it reduces the oscillation frequency by $20 %$. The value of ratio $m / M$ is close to
questions.solution:
Let $C$ be the torsional constant of the wire.

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M{\left(2L\right)}^{2}}{12}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{3C}{M . {L}^{2}}}$

After masses are attached,

${f}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M . {\left(2L\right)}^{2}}{12} + \dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{4} \times 2}}$

$⇒ 0.8f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{\left(\dfrac{M}{3} + \dfrac{m}{2}\right){L}^{2}}}$

$⇒ 0.64 \times \dfrac{3C}{M} = \dfrac{C}{\dfrac{M}{3} + \dfrac{m}{2}}$

$\left(0.64\right)M + 0.64 \times \dfrac{3}{2}m = M$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{M} = 0.37$

questions.q:
Two simple harmonic motions, as shown, are at right angles. They are combined to form Lissajous figures.
$x(t)=A \sin (a t+\delta)$y(t)=B \sin (b t)$
Identify the correct match below
options:
Parameters: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{B}, \mathrm{a}=2 \mathrm{~b} ; \delta=\frac{\pi}{2}$; Curve: Circle

Parameters: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{B}, \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{b} ; \delta=\frac{\pi}{2} ;$ Curve: Line

Parameters: $\mathrm{A} \neq \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{b} ; \delta=\frac{\pi}{2} ;$ Curve: Ellipse

Parameters: $\mathrm{A} \neq \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{b} ; \delta=0$; Curve: Parabola
questions.solution:
From the two mutually perpendicular S.H.M.'s, the general equation of Lissajous figure,

$\frac{x^2}{A^2}+\frac{y^2}{B^2}-\frac{2 x y}{A B} \cos \delta=\sin ^$2 $\delta

\begin{aligned}$&x=A \sin (a t+$\delta)$\\
&y=B \sin (b t+r)
\end{aligned}

Clearly $A \neq B$ hence ellipse.

questions.q: A body of mass $M$ and charge $q$ is connected to a spring of spring constant $k$. It is oscillating along $x$-direction about its equilibrium position in the horizontal plane, taken to be at $x = 0$, with an amplitude $A$. An electric field $E$ is applied along the $x$-direction. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The total energy of the system is  $\dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{q}^{2}{E}^{2}}{k}$
The new equilibrium position is at a distance  $\dfrac{2qE}{k}$  from  $x = 0$
The new equilibrium position is at a distance  $\dfrac{qE}{2k}$  from  $x = 0$
The total energy of the system is  $\dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{q}^{2}{E}^{2}}{k}$ .
questions.solution: The equilibrium position will shift to a point where the resultant force is equal to zero. $k{x}_{eq} = qE ⇒ {x}_{eq} = \dfrac{qE}{k}$. Energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}\left[{A}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{qE}{k}\right)}^{2}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{q}^{2}{E}^{2}}{k}$.

questions.q: A silver atom in a solid oscillates in simple harmonic motion in some direction with a frequency of ${10}^{12}{s}^{- 1}$ . What is the force constant of the bonds connecting one atom with the other? (Mole wt. of silver,$= 108g{mol}^{- 1}$ and Avogadro number $= 6.02 \times {10}^{23}$)
questions.solution:
Given, molecular weight of silver $\left(M\right) = 108g$ and Avogadro's number$\left({N}_{A}\right) = 6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}$,
frequency $\left(f\right) = {10}^{12}s$.

Mass of single silver atom will be given by,

$m = \dfrac{M}{N} = \dfrac{108}{6 . 02 \times {10}^{23}} = 1 . 79 \times {10}^{- 22}g = 1 . 79 \times {10}^{- 25}kg$

The bonds between the atoms can be considered as spring and then using the spring analog, the time period of the oscillation of the atoms is given by,

$T = \dfrac{1}{f} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$; where $k$ is spring constant.

$\dfrac{1}{{10}^{12}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\left(1 . 79 \times {10}^{- 22}\right) \times {10}^{- 3}}{k}}$

$k = 7 . 1N{m}^{- 1}$.

questions.q: A block of mass $0 . 1kg$ is connected to an elastic spring of spring constant $640N{m}^{- 1}$ and oscillates in a damping medium of damping constant ${10}^{- 2}kg{s}^{- 1}$ . The system dissipates its energy gradually. The time taken for its mechanical energy of vibration to drop to half of its initial value, is closest to-
questions.solution:
Given,

$E = \dfrac{Eo}{2}$
$⇒ A = \dfrac{Ao}{2}$
$Amplitudeofdampedoscillation = A = {A}_{o}e^{- \dfrac{bt}{2m}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{A}_{o}}{\sqrt{2}} = {A}_{o}e^{- \dfrac{bt}{2m}}$~

$\sqrt{2} = e^{\dfrac{bt}{2m}}$

$ln⁡ \left(\sqrt{2}\right) = \dfrac{bt}{2m} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 2}}{2 \times 0.1}t =\dfrac{0.1t}{2}$

$\dfrac{t}{2} =10ln ⁡ \left(\sqrt{2}\right) = 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.693$

$t = 10 \times 0.693 = 6.93$

$t \approx 7s$.

$= 5 \times {10}^{- 2}\text{cm}$

$= 0.05cm$

questions.q: The ratio of maximum acceleration to maximum velocity in a simple harmonic motion is $10{s}^{- 1} .$ At, $t = 0$ the displacement is $5m .$ What is the maximum acceleration? The initial phase is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ .
questions.solution:
In a simple harmonic motion,

Maximum acceleration, ${f}_{max} = {\omega}^{2}A$

Maximum velocity, ${v}_{max} = A\omega$.

$\dfrac{{f}_{max}}{{v}_{max}} = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2}A}{A\omega} = \omega$

$\omega = 10$

Displacement in SHM is $x = Asin ⁡ \left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

At $t = 0$

$5 = Asin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$A = 5\sqrt{2}$.

Max acceleration = ${\omega}^{2}A$

$= 100 \times 5\sqrt{2}$

$= 500\sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 2}$

$5{A}^{2} = {A}_{N}^{2} - \dfrac{4{A}^{2}}{9}$

${A}_{N}^{2} = \dfrac{49{A}^{2}}{9}$

${A}_{N} = \dfrac{7A}{3}$

questions.q: A cylindrical block of wood (density = $650kg{m}^{- 3}$), of base area $30{cm}^{2}$ and height $54cm$, floats in a liquid of density $900kg{m}^{- 3}$. The block is depressed slightly and then released. The time period of the resulting oscillations of the block would be equal to that of a simple pendulum of length (nearly) :
questions.solution:
Case-I

In equilibrium

${F}_{up} = mg$

${V}_{i}{ρ}_{L}g = mg$

$Ah{ρ}_{L}g = AL{ρ}_{s}g \ldots \ldots \ldots \left(1\right)$



Case-II

Let block is pressed by x more in liquid

${F}_{net} = {F}_{up}^{1} - mg$

$= {V}_{i}^{1}{ρ}_{L}g - mg$

${F}_{net} = A\left(h + x\right){ρ}_{L}g - AL{ρ}_{s}g$

${F}_{net} = Ah{ρ}_{L}g + Ax{ρ}_{L}g - AL{ρ}_{s}g$. . . . . . . . . . (2)

from equation (1) & (2)

${F}_{net} = Ax{ρ}_{L}g$restoring force in upward direction

$\alpha = \dfrac{{F}_{net}}{m} = \left(\dfrac{A{ρ}_{L}g}{A{ρ}_{s}L}\right)x$

$\alpha = {\omega}^{2}x for SHM$

and ${\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{g}{l}$

so $\dfrac{g}{l} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{L}g}{{ρ}_{s}L}$

so $l = \dfrac{{ρ}_{s}L}{{ρ}_{L}} = \dfrac{650 \times 54}{900} = 39cm$

questions.q: Which of the following expressions corresponds to simple harmonic motion along a straight line, where $\mathrm{x}$ is the displacement and $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ are positive constants?
questions.solution:
In linear S.H.M., the restoring force acting on particle should always be proportional to the displacement of the particle and directed towards the equilibrium position. i.e., $\mathrm{F} \propto \mathrm{x}$
or $\mathrm{F}=-\mathrm{bx}$ where $\mathrm{b}$ is a positive constant.

$A = {A}_{0} {e}^{\dfrac{- bt}{2m}}$

$b is$related to viscosity

$8 = 10{e}^{\dfrac{- {b}_{a} 40}{2m}}$

$5 = 10{e}^{\dfrac{- {b}_{C{o}_{2}} t}{2m}}$

$\dfrac{ln\dfrac{5}{4}}{ln2} = \dfrac{40}{t} \times 1.3$

$t = \dfrac{40 \times ( ln2 ) \times 1.3}{ln5 - 2ln2}$

$= \dfrac{40 \times 0.693 \times 1.3}{1.601 - 2 \times 0.693}$

$≃ 161sec$

questions.q: A particle moves with simple harmonic motion in a straight line. In first $τ s$, after starting from rest it travels a distance a, and in next $τ s$ it travels 2a, in same direction, then :
questions.solution:
$\text{x} = - A cos \omega \text{t}$

$- \text{A} + \text{a} = - \text{A cos} \omega τ$ ...(i)

$- \text{A} + 3 \text{a} = - \text{A cos} \left(\omega 2 τ\right)$ ...(ii)

$∴ - 1 + \dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{A}} = - \text\cos \omega τ$ ...(iii)

and $- 1 + \dfrac{3 \text{a}}{\text{A}} = - \text\cos \left(2 \omega τ\right)$ ...(iv)

Adding (iii) and (iv)

$2 = 3 cos \left(\omega τ\right) - 2 {\text\cos}^{2} \left(\omega τ\right) + 1$

$∴ 2 {\text\cos}^{2} \left(\omega τ\right) - 3 \text\cos \left(\omega τ\right) + 1 = 0$

$∴ \text\cos \omega τ = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \omega τ = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$∴ \text{T} = 6 τ$

and $- 1 + \dfrac{3 \text{a}}{\text{A}} = - \text\cos \left(2 \omega τ\right)$ ...(iv)

Adding (iii) and (iv)

$2 = 3 cos \left(\omega τ\right) - 2 {\text\cos}^{2} \left(\omega τ\right) + 1$

$∴ 2 {\text\cos}^{2} \left(\omega τ\right) - 3 \text\cos \left(\omega τ\right) + 1 = 0$

$∴ \omega τ = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.q: Two simple pendulums of length $1 \mathrm{~m}$ and $4 \mathrm{~m}$ respectively are both given small displacement in the same direction at the same instant. They will be again in phase after the shorter pendulum has completed number of oscillations equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $T_1 and T_2$ be the time period of the two pendulums $\mathrm{T}_1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{~g}}}$ and $\mathrm{T}_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{4}{\mathrm{~g}}}$ As $\ell_1 \lt  \ell_2$ therefore $\mathrm{T}_1 \lt  \mathrm{T}_2$ Let at $\mathrm{t}=0$ they start swinging together. Since their time periods are different, the swinging will not be in unison always. Only when number of completed oscillations
differ by an integer, the two pendulums will again begin to swing together Let longer length pendulum complete $\mathrm{n}$ oscillation and shorter length pendulum complete $(n+1)$ oscillation. For unison swinging

$\begin{aligned}$& (n+1) T_1=n_2 \\
& (n+1) $\times$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{1}{g}}=($n) $\times$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{4}{g}}$\\
& \Rightarrow n=1 \\
& \therefore n+1=1+1=2
\end{aligned}

& \Rightarrow n=1 \\
& \therefore n+1=1+1=2
\end{aligned}$

Assuming that the system is completely isolated from its surrounding, the piston executes a simple harmonic motion with frequency
[Assume the system is in space.]
questions.solution:
For an adiabatic process,

${\text{Pv}}^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$

Differentiating with respect to $v$,

$\dfrac{\text{dP}}{\text{dv}}\left({\text{v}}^{\gamma}\right) + P\gamma{\text{v}}^{\gamma - 1} = 0$

$\text{dP} = \dfrac{- \gamma P}{\text{v}}\text{dv} = \dfrac{- \gamma P}{\text{v}}\text{Adx}$



Thus, the acceleration, $\text{a} = \dfrac{\text{dF}}{\text{M}} = \dfrac{\gamma{\text{PA}}^{2}}{\text{MV}}\text{dx}$

Comparing with , $\text{a} = - {\omega}^{2}\text{dx}$, we get,

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma{P}_{0}{A}^{2}}{M{V}_{0}}} = 2\pif$


$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma{P}_{0}{A}^{2}}{M{V}_{0}}}$

questions.q: If a simple pendulum has significant amplitude (up to a factor of $1 / e$ of original) only in the period between $t=0s$ to $t=\tau s$, then $\tau$ may be called the average life of the pendulum. When the spherical bob of the pendulum suffers a retardation (due to viscous drag) proportional to its velocity, with '$b$' as the constant of proportionality, the average life time of the pendulum is (assuming damping is small) in seconds:
questions.solution: As retardation $=\mathrm{bv}$\therefore$ retarding force $=\mathrm{mbv}$\therefore$ net restoring torque when angular displacement is $\theta$ is given by $=-\operatorname{mg} \ell \sin \theta+\operatorname{mbv} \ell$\therefore \quad \mathrm{I} \alpha=-m g \ell \sin \theta+\operatorname{mbv} \ell$ where, $\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{m} \ell^2$\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^2}=\alpha=-\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\ell} \sin \theta+\frac{\mathrm{bv}}{\ell}$ for small damping, the solution of the above differential equation will be $\therefore \quad \theta=\theta_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{bt}}{2}} \sin (w t+\phi)$\therefore \quad$ angular amplitude will be $=\theta . e^{\frac{-b t}{2}}$ According to question, in $\tau$ time (average life-time), angular amplitude drops to $\frac{1}{e}$ value of its original value $(\theta)$\therefore \quad \frac{\theta_0}{\mathrm{e}}=\theta_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{6 \tau}{2}}$\frac{6 \tau}{2}=1$\therefore \quad \tau=\frac{2}{b}$
